facts.quote:
AI literacy should be understood as a complement to, 
not a substitute for, developer responsibility, institutional safeguards and regulatory accountability.
facts.summary: The preliminary report identifies gaps in AI literacy frameworks, independent evaluation and adoption across schools and professional training. It treats literacy as institutional capacity building alongside developer and regulatory responsibility.
facts.document_status: Preliminary scientific assessment, July 2026; not an adopted education programme.

facts.quote:
Oversight 
is not yet operationalized as a measurable 
requirement with concrete expectations for 
intervention, reversibility and accountability
facts.summary: The report identifies a governance capacity gap for autonomous agents and calls for measurable human oversight, evaluation and interoperability standards, critical-infrastructure collaboration, and clearer attribution in liability and incident reporting.
facts.document_status: Preliminary scientific assessment of institutional preparedness needs.

facts.quote:
National strategies to address disinformation 
and persuasion are an exception.
facts.summary: The report identifies limited national preparedness for AI-enabled persuasion and disinformation, arguing that governance must address the incentives and infrastructure that make manipulation profitable as well as content moderation.
facts.document_status: Preliminary scientific assessment, July 2026; not evidence of a new adopted national strategy.

facts.quote:
Human rights due diligence, impact 
assessments and rights-by-design approaches 
provide established tools
facts.summary: The report frames human-rights and child-rights impact assessment as existing instruments that can be applied across the AI lifecycle, while identifying transparency and explainability gaps that impede accountability and remedies.
facts.document_status: Preliminary scientific assessment of available governance tools.
